exposure: Intracaesarian placement of intrauterine contraceptive device (IUCD)
Interval placement of intrauterine contraceptive device (IUCD) at 6 weeks postpartum
outcome: Continued use of IUCD at 6 months postpartum
cohort: One hundred and four pregnant women aged 20 to 40 years old, planned for an elective caesarian delivery, and who opted for an intrauterine contraceptive device were included.
finding: Intracaesarian placement of an intrauterine contraceptive device leads to statistically significantly higher continuation rates at 6 months postpartum compared to conventional interval placement, with no statistically significant difference in expulsion rates.
mod_finding: The study found that intracaesarian placement of an IUCD resulted in higher continuation rates compared to interval placement.
